title: Affine Decision-Tree Leaf Complexity of Balanced Boolean Functions
summary: The minimum affine decision-tree leaf count is trivially at most two to the n; characterize its worst-case behavior over balanced Boolean functions and prove a nontrivial upper bound.

formal_statement.body: Characterize $L_n=\max_{f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2\,\mathrm{balanced}}\operatorname{minLeaves}(f)$ and prove a nontrivial upper bound on $L_n$.

scope.domain: Boolean-function complexity, specifically affine decision-tree leaf complexity for balanced Boolean functions.
parameters: L_n: maximum minLeaves value over balanced n-bit Boolean functions, measuring worst-case affine decision-tree leaf complexity
scope.unresolved_remainder: Characterize L_n and prove a nontrivial upper bound on it.

progress.summary: The paper presents the general behavior of the minimum leaf count as an interesting problem and specifically calls for a nontrivial upper bound. It reports structural properties and small-dimensional computations but no general nontrivial upper bound.
citation_labels: Marek Broll et al., Generic Framework for Key-Guessing Improvements
